newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Manuel says stable policy best defence for SA rand.
newsitem.headline: Manuel says stable policy best defence for SA rand.

text.p: Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Wednesday the proper response to the falling value of the South African rand lay in the steady implementation of the government's announced macro-economic strategy.
The rand fell to a new low of 4.74 rand to the dollar on Wednesday, a decline of over 30 percent since February.

"Clearly, the adequate response relates to the implementation of the macro-economic strategy. It's not chopping and changing. It's not trying to hold your own against speculation," Manuel said during a parliamentary debate.

Opposition Democratic Party finance spokesman Ken Andrew said Manuel should immediately abolish remaining exchange controls, a move seen by many foreign investors as a guage of the government's confidence in its own economy.

"South Africa should abolish all foreign exchange controls immediately and our foreign reserves should not be used at all to prop up the exchange rate. We should take our medicine now in one big swallow rather than prolong the agony," he said.

Manuel did not respond directly to Andrew's call or to Wednesday's further slide in the value of the rand, but said South Africa's priority should be to get the economic fundamentals in place and tackle the budget deficit.

"Clearly we want to curb the government deficit and the level of government dissaving, to avoid permanent increases in the overall tax burden, to reduce goverment consumption expenditure relative to GDP, to strengthen the government's contribution to gross domestic fixed investment.
"The overal objective is to address the structural deficit, which is a medium-term strategy," he said.
Manuel said the government was on target to reduce the deficit to 5.1 percent in fiscal 1996/97 and to four percent in the next financial year.
